strategies.comments:
Other Options

A mixed set taps into Exploud's solid special coverage to beat Wormadam-S and Lairon and still allows it to dent specially defensive Pokemon like Clefairy and Muk with STAB Return. However, not fully investing in one of Exploud's attacking stats makes it less effective as a wallbreaker, as physically defensive Clefairy, Hippopotas, and Vibrava will wall Exploud. Work Up might seem interesting to power up Exploud's moves and make it an even more effective wallbreaker with the flexibility to switch between its moves, but its defensive vulnerability creates few windows to set up and leaves it vulnerable to revenge killers.

Checks and Counters

Faster Offensive Pokemon: Exploud's underwhelming bulk and middling Speed leave it prone to being revenge killed by everything from Persian and Emolga to Glaceon and Kingler. Pokemon with Fighting-type coverage like Mr. Mime, Grumpig, and Simisear can threaten to OHKO Exploud, and Jolly Mienfoo sets can do the same.

Special Walls: Depending on its set, Exploud may be unable to 2HKO Clefairy, and losing its power-boosting item to Knock Off will leave it more easily walled. Clefairy can heal off damage Exploud inflicts, is only threatened by Focus Blast and Choice Band Return, and may slow Exploud down further with Thunder Wave. Other special walls like Munchlax, Hypno, and Grumpig do well against Exploud's special attacking set, but they struggle to handle the power of its Choice Band set.

Steel- and Rock-types: Lairon, Solrock, and Wormadam-S deter Choice Band Exploud from spamming Return, though they are hit hard by its coverage moves and can be surprised by the specially offensive set.

movesets.name: Special Attacker
movesets.description:
Exploud's good Special Attack and colorful coverage make it a decent wallbreaker in BW ZU. Surf threatens Rock-types that resist Hyper Voice like Solrock, Lairon, and Graveler, easily threatening to KO them or bring Graveler down to Sturdy. Fire Blast obliterates Wormadam-S, which is otherwise an excellent check to Normal-types, and easily OHKOes Pawniard; Fire Blast also 2HKOes Meganium, a common special wall that isn't 2HKOed by Hyper Voice. Focus Blast 2HKOes Clefairy, which is otherwise one of the best special walls in BW ZU, and can even 3HKO mixed wall Munchlax. Scrappy makes Exploud's STAB-boosted Hyper Voice unable to be taken advantage of by Ghost-types like Frillish, Lampent, and Gastly, making it especially spammable. A Modest nature maximizes Exploud's power and still enables it to outspeed defensive Pokemon. A Life Orb lets Exploud maximize its coverage options. Choice Specs leans into Exploud's spammable STAB Hyper Voice, threatening more KOs, such as against offensive Shelgon after Stealth Rock damage, and it lacks the drawback of recoil damage that can leave Exploud more easily revenge killed.

Exploud fits balance teams as a slower wallbreaker that appreciates support from pivots. Persian is an excellent partner for Exploud, luring in defensive Pokemon like Solrock, Wormadam-S, and Lairon for Exploud to destroy using its coverage. Exploud threatening Persian's checks better enables Persian to clean up weakened teams. Persian can also U-turn more freely given Exploud pressures the aforementioned Stealth Rock setters. Lopunny similarly lures in defensive Pokemon, and it brings additional utility like Thunder Wave and Healing Wish to mitigate Exploud's low Speed and poor bulk, respectively. Exploud's lacking defensive profile means it struggles to switch in easily, so it thrives with support from pivots such as Emolga and Mienfoo. Fast offensive Pokemon like Simisear, Mr. Mime, and Raichu excel at cleaning up weakened teams that Exploud punched holes into, and they compensate for its middling Speed against revenge killers. Choice Scarf users like Grumpig and Glaceon can threaten common fast revenge killers like Persian and Emolga, and they benefit from Exploud softening up special walls like Clefairy and Munchlax. Lairon and Graveler are great defensive answers to Emolga and Persian for Exploud, and the support they offer with Stealth Rock makes Exploud more punishing to switch around. Exploud is slower than Jolly Mienfoo, so it appreciates support from checks to it like Muk and Arbok, both of which appreciate Exploud pressuring physically defensive Pokemon like Solrock, Hippopotas, and Graveler. Pokemon like Meganium and Grumpig can stomach special Fighting-type coverage moves that threaten Exploud.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Unlike the more common, faster physically offensive Normal-types like Persian, Slaking, and Lopunny, Exploud is strong, can spam its STAB moves thanks to Scrappy, and has a wide array of coverage moves. Low Kick demolishes the few Pokemon that could otherwise take more than 2 Returns, namely Lairon, Graveler, and Pawniard. Crunch 2HKOes the most common physical wall in ZU: Solrock, which would otherwise easily take Return and Low Kick. Fire Punch OHKOes Wormadam-S, which is a very important target despite Fire Punch's complete lack of use otherwise. Earthquake is an option that hits uncommon Normal-resistant foes like Corsola, Magcargo, and Magnemite, all of which don't take much damage from Low Kick. Choice Band Exploud should run an Adamant nature to maximize its damage output, even at the cost of not outspeeding foes like Jolly Mienfoo, Timid Walrein, and Choice Specs Glaceon, as Exploud should aim to break slower Pokemon.

Choice Band Exploud excels at breaking holes in teams, so it's a good fit for offensive teams wanting for a consistent and strong wallbreaker. Faster offensive Pokemon like Emolga, Simisear, and Raichu can clean up teams that have been ravaged by Exploud. Setup sweepers like Shelgon, Whiscash, and Rock Polish Lairon have an easier time sweeping thanks to Exploud removing or weakening physically defensive Pokemon like Lairon, Vullaby, and Leafeon. Exploud's poor defensive utility prevents it from switching in safely, so slower pivots like Vibrava, Pelipper, and Mienfoo support Exploud well by positioning it to break slower defensive Pokemon they lure in like Meganium, Clefairy, and Muk. Faster pivots like Persian and Emolga also tend to lure in slow defensive Pokemon like Lairon, Solrock, and Graveler for Exploud to threaten, and by removing or weakening these threats, Exploud can set its faster partners up to effectively clean teams. Exploud's mediocre Speed and terrible defensive typing are a bad combination that leave it easily revenge killed, so it's very dependent on defensive Pokemon like Wormadam-S, Meganium, and Solrock to protect it from faster attackers.

strategies.overview: Exploud has only one role in the NU metagame, and that is being a specially based wallbreaker. Scrappy allows Exploud to break through the Ghost-types that trouble most Normal-type attackers without missing a beat. With a decent offensive movepool rich with coverage options and above average attacking stats, it would seem like it excels at this role. Sadly, while it has the right moves to threaten many defensive Pokemon, its offenses are just shy of being powerful in comparison to the average offensive threat. Exploud's low Speed and mediocre defenses are another sour note, as it cannot stand against the power of offensive teams. Together, these factors usually make Exploud a liability in NU's fast-paced metagame.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Exploud has a decent movepool that contains interesting options such as Shadow Ball, Extrasensory, and Icy Wind, but the moves already listed are usually the best options. Taunt can be useful to allow Exploud to act as an anti-lead and also disrupt stall teams though. Expert Belt can be used to boost Exploud's moves without causing recoil, but Life Orb's boost is generally superior because Exploud doesn't take attacks very well and Expert Belt doesn't boost its STAB. Choice Specs can also be used, but Exploud is very weak for a Choice Specs attacker and appreciates being able to change moves. Soundproof is somewhat helpful on Baton Pass chains, as the ability gives Exploud a helpful immunity to Roar and Perish Song.

Checks and Counters

Specially defensive Altaria is a decent counter if Exploud lacks Ice Beam, as it isn't 2HKOed by any other move. Fighting-types such as Sawk and Primeape easily OHKO Exploud, though most can't safely switch in. Gurdurr is a notable exception, as it can take any hit thanks to its good bulk and recover with Drain Punch. While it has excellent neutral coverage against most of the tier, Exploud is not that powerful, so many Pokemon can simply take a hit and retaliate back hard. As Exploud is relatively slow and frail, most offensive Pokemon can easily outspeed and take it out.

movesets.name: Wallbreaker
movesets.description:
Exploud's above average attacking stats make it a viable wallbreaker. Hyper Voice provides Exploud with STAB and works well in conjunction with Scrappy to deter Ghost-types from switching in. Surf hits the Rock-types that resist Hyper Voice, while Fire Blast targets Steel-types. Low Kick takes advantage of Exploud's usable Attack and hits several of the special walls that take Exploud's other moves easily, most notably Lickilicky and Regice.

The power boost provided by Life Orb makes it the only viable item. With Life Orb, Exploud can 2HKO Lickilicky after Stealth Rock damage with Low Kick. The Speed EVs allow Exploud to outspeed Modest Ludicolo. Unfortunately, it is unable to outspeed Timid Ludicolo or any other mildly fast attacker, making it vulnerable to offensive teams. Hammer Arm is a very viable option over Low Kick because it can inflict more damage upon Audino and Zweilous, but the Speed drop means that Exploud will still lose to Miltank. Ice Beam can hit Altaria hard, but it doesn't have much use otherwise. Entry hazard setters are very useful for Exploud to make up for its average power. Golurk and Seismitoad are good teammates to set up Stealth Rock, which allows Exploud to gain KOs on Misdreavus, Lickilicky, and Torkoal. Garbodor and Roselia are good Spikes users, giving Exploud the opportunity to score KOs on several Pokemon, including Golurk, Bastiodon, and Alomomola. Pokemon that enjoy the removal of physical walls are good teammates for Exploud, with Kangaskhan, Golurk, and Samurott being good examples. Fighting-types, such as Sawk and Primeape, are notable for appreciating Exploud's ability to beat Misdreavus and Weezing. Teammates that can handle opposing Fighting-types, such as Musharna and Misdreavus, are very beneficial. Misdreavus is especially helpful because it can also act as a spinblocker to prevent the entry hazards Exploud benefits from being easily removed.
